topics.title: Comparing Objects and Finding Similarities & Differences
topics.concept:
What is Comparing?

Comparing means looking at two or more things to see how they are the same or different. We compare by size, shape, colour, weight, length, and other properties.

Ways to Compare Objects:

PropertyHow to CompareWords We Use
**Size**Which is bigger or smaller?big, small, bigger, smaller
**Length**Which is longer or shorter?long, short, longer, shorter
**Height**Which is taller or shorter?tall, short, taller, shorter
**Weight**Which is heavier or lighter?heavy, light, heavier, lighter
**Colour**Are they the same colour?same, different
**Shape**Are they the same shape?same, different

What are Similarities?

Similarities are ways that objects are the same. For example, a red apple and a red ball are similar because they are both red.

What are Differences?

Differences are ways that objects are different. For example, an apple and a ball are different because one is fruit, one is a toy.

Questions to Ask When Comparing:

  • What is the same about these objects?
  • What is different about these objects?
  • Which one is bigger/smaller/longer/shorter?
  • How are they alike?

examples.problem: Compare a cat and a dog. Name one similarity and one difference.
examples.solution:
• Similarity: Both are pets, both have 4 legs, both have fur
  • Difference: Cats meow, dogs bark; cats have whiskers, etc.

-

Answer: Similarity: Both are pets; Difference: Cats meow, dogs bark **Example 2:** Which is heavier: a feather or a rock? *Solution:* - A feather is very light - A rock is much heavier - **Answer:** Rock is heavier **Example 3:** A red crayon and a blue crayon. How are they the same? How are they different? *Solution:* - Same: Both are crayons, same shape, same size (if same brand) - Different: Different colours (red vs blue) - **Answer:** Same: both crayons; Different: different colours

recap: Comparing means looking at how things are alike or different
Similarities are things that are the SAME
Compare by: size, length, height, weight, colour, shape
Always look for both similarities AND differences

topics.title: Sorting, Grouping, and Sequencing Activities
topics.concept:
What is Sorting?

Sorting means putting objects into groups based on a rule. For example, putting all red blocks together and all blue blocks together.

What is Grouping?

Grouping is similar to sorting. We put things that are alike into the same group.

Rules for Sorting and Grouping:

RuleGroup AGroup B
By colourAll red thingsAll blue things
By shapeAll circlesAll squares
By sizeBig thingsSmall things
By useToysBooks
By typeFruitsVegetables

What is Sequencing?

Sequencing means putting things in a specific order. For example, putting numbers in order from smallest to largest.

Types of Sequences:

TypeExamplePattern
Size orderSmall → Medium → LargeGetting bigger
Time orderMorning → Afternoon → EveningTime of day
Number order1, 2, 3, 4, 5Counting up
Alphabet orderA, B, C, DLetters
Event orderFirst → Next → LastStory order

examples.problem: Sort these items into two groups: Apple, Carrot, Banana, Broccoli
examples.solution:
• Group 1 (Fruits): Apple, Banana
  • Group 2 (Vegetables): Carrot, Broccoli

-

Answer: Fruits: Apple, Banana; Vegetables: Carrot, Broccoli **Example 2:** What comes next in this sequence? 5, 10, 15, ___ *Solution:* - Pattern: Add 5 each time - 15 + 5 = 20 - **Answer:** 20 **Example 3:** Arrange these in order from shortest to tallest: Giraffe, Mouse, Dog, Cat *Solution:* - Shortest: Mouse - Next: Cat - Next: Dog - Tallest: Giraffe - **Answer:** Mouse, Cat, Dog, Giraffe

recap: Sorting = putting things into groups by a rule
Common sequences: size, time, numbers, alphabet
Look for the pattern to find what comes next

topics.title: Puzzle Solving and Logical Thinking Games
topics.concept:
What is a Puzzle?

A puzzle is a problem that makes you think. You use clues and logic to find the answer. Puzzles are fun and help your brain grow!

What is Logical Thinking?

Logical thinking means using facts and clues to figure something out. You put the pieces of information together to find the answer.

Types of Logic Puzzles:

TypeWhat You DoExample
**What comes next?**Find the pattern🔴🔵🔴🔵___ (next is 🔴)
**Odd one out**Find the different one🍎🍌🍊🥕 (🥕 is different)
**Matching**Pair things that go togetherSock → Shoe
**Riddles**Solve using clues"I have 4 legs and say meow" → Cat
**Order puzzles**Put in correct orderFirst, next, last

Tips for Solving Puzzles:

1. Read all the clues carefully

2. Look for patterns

3. Think about what you already know

4. Try one idea, then another

5. Don't give up - practice makes better!

Logical Thinking Games to Play:

  • Pattern matching games
  • Memory matching cards
  • "What doesn't belong?" games
  • Simple Sudoku (with shapes/colours)
  • Following directions games

• Pattern: Star, Star with tail, Star, Star with tail...
  • The pattern repeats every 2: ★ then ☆
  • After ★ comes ☆

-

Answer: ☆ **Example 2:** Find the odd one out: Triangle, Square, Circle, Book *Solution:* - Triangle, Square, Circle are all shapes - Book is not a shape (it is an object) - **Answer:** Book **Example 3:** Solve the riddle: "I have pages but I am not a tree. You read me. What am I?" *Solution:* - Has pages ✓ - Not a tree ✓ - You read it ✓ - **Answer:** A book

recap: Puzzles make you think and solve problems
Logical thinking uses clues to find answers
Look for patterns in "what comes next" puzzles
Find the odd one out by spotting differences
Riddles give clues to guess the answer
Practice puzzles to get better at logical thinking

questions.q: Which is heavier: a pillow or a brick?
questions.explanation: Brick is heavier than a pillow

questions.q: Find the odd one out: Apple, Banana, Carrot, Orange
questions.explanation: Carrot is a vegetable; others are fruits

questions.q: Sort these by colour: Red ball, Blue car, Red apple, Blue bird
options: Red: ball, apple; Blue: car, bird
Red: car, bird; Blue: ball, apple
Red: ball, car; Blue: apple, bird
questions.explanation: Red objects: ball and apple; Blue: car and bird

questions.q: Which is taller: a giraffe or a cat?
questions.explanation: Giraffes are very tall; cats are short

questions.q: Put in order from smallest to largest: Elephant, Mouse, Dog
questions.explanation: Mouse smallest, then dog, then elephant

questions.q: Solve the riddle: "I have 2 wheels. You ride me. What am I?"
questions.explanation: Bicycle has 2 wheels and you ride it

questions.q: What is the similarity between a circle and a square?
questions.explanation: Circle and square are both shapes

questions.q: Complete the sequence: Morning, Afternoon, ___ , Night

questions.explanation: All others are even numbers; 7 is odd

questions.q: If all circles are red, and this shape is a circle, what colour is it?
questions.explanation: All circles are red, so this circle is red

questions.q: Arrange in order from earliest to latest: Dinner, Lunch, Breakfast, Snack
questions.explanation: Morning→Breakfast, then Lunch, then Snack, then Dinner

questions.q: Which word does NOT belong? Table, Chair, Sofa, Apple
questions.explanation: Apple is food; others are furniture
